For a \(3\times3\) matrix it is \(|A|^2\) — students who answer \(|A|\) (forgetting the power) or \(|A|^3\) (over-counting) walk into the two standard distractors.

\(\operatorname{adj}(AB) = \operatorname{adj}B\,\operatorname{adj}A\) — the order REVERSES: Like transpose and inverse, the adjoint of a product flips the factors: \(\operatorname{adj}(AB) = \operatorname{adj}B\,\operatorname{adj}A\), not \(\operatorname{adj}A\,\operatorname{adj}B\). Keeping the original order is the trap.
